title: A Door in the Oak
story:
Noor was looking for a quiet place to read in the park. She sat under a huge oak and leaned against the trunk. A small round door was set into the bark near the roots. It was no taller than her hand, and it had a brass handle. Noor knocked twice, because knocking felt more polite than pulling. The door opened, and a tiny gardener stepped out.

He wore a green cap and carried a watering can the size of a spoon. He said his flowers were thirsty after a long dry week. He asked Noor to fetch three drops from the park fountain. In return, he promised her a seed that glowed at night. Noor agreed and walked to the fountain with great care. She caught three drops on a clean leaf and hurried back. The gardener watered three blue flowers, and they lifted their heads. He placed a warm seed in Noor's palm and bowed. He told her to plant it in a cup of soil by a window. Noor thanked him, and the little door closed without a sound.

At home, she planted the seed before supper. That night, a soft gold light rose from the cup. It was bright enough to read one page, then it dimmed. Noor smiled and decided to visit the oak again on Sunday.
